children: Higher yields now provide a substantially better income buffer than in recent years, while cash remains exposed to inflation and reinvestment risk, Julius Baer's Afonso Borges says in a note. A disorderly bond crisis is unlikely, according to Julius Baer. Within fixed income, Julius Baer favors high-quality investment-grade corporate bonds in the five-to-10-year segment, where carry and roll-down potential compensate investors without excessive exposure to a fiscal-driven rise in long-end term premia, the fixed income analyst says. Julius Baer complements this allocation with U.S. Treasury inflation protected securities and real assets as protection against a less orderly fiscal adjustment. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)
